    # rows are the result, not working space; the old side renders
    # nothing. Returns (worst_sid, worst_num, worst_den, all_reachable,
    # no_over, rows) with the no-failure tag represented by worst_sid
    # None. Extra space is just the one live scenario: O(KV + FV + A).
    worst_sid = None
    worst_num, worst_den = 0, 1
    all_reachable = True
    no_over = True
    rows = []
    for rec in _config_compound_iter(nodes, links, flows, flow_count,
                                     prepared):
        sid, paths, costs, used, peak, reachable, over = rec
        num, den = peak
        if num * worst_den > worst_num * den:
            worst_sid, worst_num, worst_den = sid, num, den
        if not reachable:
            all_reachable = False
        if over:
            no_over = False
        if render:
            flow_rows = [[item[0], costs[i],
                          [] if paths[i] is None else paths[i]]
                         for i, item in enumerate(flows)]
            link_rows = []
            for index, link in enumerate(links):
                u = used[index]
                link_rows.append([link["from"], link["to"],
                                  link["bandwidth"], u,
                                  _config_capacity_six(u,
                                                       link["bandwidth"])])
            rows.append([sid, _config_capacity_six(num, den),
                         reachable and not over, flow_rows, link_rows])
    return (worst_sid, worst_num, worst_den, all_reachable, no_over,
            rows)


def _config_compound_impact(old_sid, old_num, old_den,
                            new_sid, new_num, new_den, scenario_rows):
    # Build the [oldWorst, newWorst, delta, scenarios] impact row from
    # each side's selected worst and the already-rendered new-side
    # scenario rows. A worst is [scenarioId, peak] with scenarioId null
    # for the no-failure scenario else the scenario id string, peak a
    # six-decimal half-up string of the exact rational scenario peak;
    # delta is the signed six-decimal newWorst-oldWorst.
    return [[old_sid, _config_capacity_six(old_num, old_den)],
            [new_sid, _config_capacity_six(new_num, new_den)],
            _config_capacity_delta_six(new_num, new_den, old_num, old_den),
            scenario_rows]


def _config_compound_gate_batch(pack_path, pack, v, history, mode, base,
                                events, flows, limit_ppm, scenario_specs):
    # Batched hotload with a per-event compound-failure capacity gate
    # (config op 26): [26, m, b, E, F, S, L]. m is 0 (read-only preview)
    # or 1 (atomic commit); b the caller-observed base version; E a
    # non-empty array of non-decreasing-clock [e, t, p] events exactly
    # like op 16's; F a non-empty array of [id, source, destination,
    # demand] flows shaped exactly like op 24's; S a non-empty array of
    # [id, nodes, links] compound-failure scenarios with unique
    # non-empty string ids, unique existing failed nodes that no flow
    # uses as an endpoint, and unique directed explicit [from, to]
    # failure links, validated against h[b] (an explicit link may not
    # touch the scenario's failed nodes and the resulting failure sets
    # may not repeat); L a non-boolean integer in 0..1000000, the
    # largest allowed worst-utilization increase as a fraction of one
    # million. Failure objects an earlier candidate deleted are
    # unavailable on that later side and simply drop out of its
    # scenario routing.
    #
    # Every input validates first (shapes in the command entry; the h[b]
    # reference/endpoint/scenario checks, clocks, and event t/p here),
    # then simulation walks from h[b] in E order. For each compared side
    # the flows are routed in scenario order: the no-failure scenario
    # first and then each S scenario in order, with its failed nodes,
    # their associated links, and its explicit failure links removed. A
    # scenario routes each flow on the lowest-cost available path with
    # shortest_paths' full-node-sequence Unicode tie break; a link's
    # used is the summed demand of the flows traversing it and the
    # scenario peak is the exact maximum used/bandwidth; the worst
    # scenario is the largest peak, an equal peak broken by no-failure
    # then S order. Any unreachable flow or overloaded link in an
    # old-side scenario - including every scenario at h[b] - is code 5.
    #
    # An event whose t/p equals the previous state is idempotent (row
    # status 1, no version, an empty impact). Every other event fails
    # when any new-side scenario has an unreachable flow or an
    # overloaded link, or when the exact worst-peak increase exceeds
    # L/1000000 (integer cross multiplication only, never floats). A
    # passing event (row status 0, a candidate version) and the first
    # failing event alike carry the impact
    # [oldWorst, newWorst, delta, scenarios] with a worst
    # [scenarioId, peak] (scenarioId null for no failure else the
    # scenario id string) and scenarios listing only the new side as
    # [scenarioId, peak, pass, flows, links]; flows are
    # [id, cost, path] ([id, null, []] when unreachable) and links
    # [from, to, bandwidth, used, utilization] in topology order, the
    # ratios six-decimal half-up strings and delta signed. At the first
    # failing event simulation stops at once and the whole batch
    # rejects: batch status 2, old/new both the pre-call v, applied
    # false, config the pre-call pack, and PACK untouched in either
    # mode.
    #
    # Once every event is a gated candidate, version/history append,
    # duplicate-resend recognition, the preview/commit difference, and
    # the single atomic replace follow op 16 exactly. For B events, S
    # scenarios, K distinct flow sources, F flows, V nodes, and A links
    # the bound is O(B(S+1)(K(V^2+A) + FV + A)) time and
    # O(KV + FV + A) extra space besides the returned result.
    if base > v:
        fail(5)
    base_topo = history[base][1]
    base_node_set = set(base_topo["nodes"])
    for item in flows:
        if item[1] not in base_node_set or item[2] not in base_node_set:
            fail(5)
    prepared = _config_compound_prepare(base_topo["nodes"],
                                        base_topo["links"], flows,
                                        scenario_specs)
    last_e = None
    for item in events:
        e = item[0]
        if last_e is not None and e < last_e:
            fail(5)
        last_e = e
        _validate_topology(item[1], metrics=True)
        if not _is_policy(item[2]):
            fail(5)

    flow_count = len(flows)
    cur_version = base
    cur_t = history[base][1]
    cur_p = history[base][2]
    (cur_worst_sid, cur_worst_num, cur_worst_den,
     cur_reachable, cur_no_over, _) = _config_compound_assess(
         cur_t["nodes"], cur_t["links"], flows, flow_count, prepared,
         False)
    # The batch is only defined from a failure-feasible h[b]: every
    # flow must be routable in every scenario and every link within its
    # bandwidth there.
    if not cur_reachable or not cur_no_over:
        fail(5)

    rows = []
    suffix = []
    for event in events:
        e, new_t, new_p = event
        if new_t == cur_t and new_p == cur_p:
            rows.append([e, 1, cur_version, cur_version, []])
            continue
        if cur_version >= MAX_COST:
            fail(5)
        (new_worst_sid, new_worst_num, new_worst_den,
         new_reachable, new_no_over, scenario_rows) = \
            _config_compound_assess(new_t["nodes"], new_t["links"],
                                    flows, flow_count, prepared, True)
        passed = new_reachable and new_no_over
        if passed:
            # Exact comparison of the worst-peak increase against
            # L/1000000: newWorst - oldWorst <= L/1000000.

                - cur_worst_num * new_worst_den

                           <= limit_ppm * new_worst_den * cur_worst_den)
            if not increase_ok:
                passed = False

            cur_worst_sid, cur_worst_num, cur_worst_den,
            new_worst_sid, new_worst_num, new_worst_den, scenario_rows)

            rows.append([e, 2, cur_version, cur_version, impact])

                    "new": v, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                    "config": pack}
        next_version = cur_version + 1
        rows.append([e, 0, cur_version, next_version, impact])
        suffix.append([next_version, new_t, new_p])
        cur_version = next_version
        cur_t, cur_p = new_t, new_p
        cur_worst_sid = new_worst_sid
        cur_worst_num, cur_worst_den = new_worst_num, new_worst_den

        # already end exactly at the simulated suffix with every entry
        # equal; anything else is a version/suffix conflict.
        if change_count == 0 or v != base + change_count:
            fail(5)
        for offset, entry in enumerate(suffix, start=1):
            if history[base + offset] != entry:
                fail(5)
        return {"op": 26, "mode": mode, "status": 1, "old": base,
                "new": v, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                "config": pack}

    if change_count == 0:
        # All events idempotent at the current version: nothing to
        # append, so a commit writes nothing either.
        return {"op": 26, "mode": mode, "status": 0, "old": base,
                "new": base, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                "config": pack}
    new_pack = {"v": v + change_count, "t": cur_t, "p": cur_p,
                "h": history + suffix}
    if mode == 1:
        _write_state_atomic(pack_path, new_pack)
        applied = True
    else:
        applied = False
    return {"op": 26, "mode": mode, "status": 0, "old": base,
            "new": v + change_count, "applied": applied, "events": rows,
            "config": new_pack}

                         out_path):

    # a non-empty list of [e, r, o, n, a] items: e is a non-decreasing

    # the target — and writes L to OUT in the canonical byte form via
    # one atomic replace, or nothing when OUT already holds those bytes
    # (status 1); PACK is never touched. mode 1 (O null) validates the
    # same way, ignores the a=false items, and for each commit either
    # verifies h[n] against the target when n is already in h or
    # appends [n, t, p] consecutively from v+1, replacing PACK
    # atomically once; replaying the same L again only verifies, so
    # repeated replays are idempotent (status 1, no write). steps

    # with S the total input/output size.

        fail(5)
    sim_history = [list(entry) for entry in history]
    steps = []
    applied = 0
    prev_e = None
    prev_o = None
    prev_n = None
    prev_a = None
    for item in log:
        e, r, o, n, a = item

            fail(5)
        expected_o = base if prev_o is None \
            else (prev_n if prev_a else prev_o)
        if o != expected_o or r > o:

        target_t, target_p = sim_history[r][1], sim_history[r][2]
        if sim_history[o][1] == target_t and sim_history[o][2] == target_p:

def _config_latency_gate_batch(pack_path, pack, v, history, mode, base,
                               events, flows, limit_ppm, moved_ppm):
    # Batched hotload with a per-event latency-bounded reroute gate
    # (config op 23): [23, m, b, E, F, L, C]. m is 0 (read-only preview)
    # or 1 (atomic commit); b the caller-observed base version; E a
    # non-empty array of non-decreasing-clock [e, t, p] events exactly
    # like op 16's; F a non-empty array of
    # [id, source, destination, demand, maxLatency] flows with unique
    # non-empty string ids, two distinct endpoints that are both nodes
    # of the h[b] topology, a demand a non-boolean integer in
    # 1..MAX_COST, and a maxLatency a non-boolean integer in
    # 0..MAX_TIME; L a non-boolean integer in 0..1000000, the largest
    # allowed peak-increase as a fraction of one million; C a
    # non-boolean integer in 0..1000000, the largest rerouted demand as
    # a fraction of total demand.
    #
    # Every input validates first (shapes in the command entry; the h[b]
    # endpoint check, clocks, and event t/p here), then simulation walks
    # from h[b] in E order. Every flow is routed on the up-link
    # lowest-cost path with shortest_paths' full-node-sequence Unicode
    # tie break, exactly like op 22, with the path latency the sum of
    # its link latencies; a reachable path whose latency sum exceeds
    # MAX_TIME is code 5. The batch is only defined from a feasible
    # h[b]: every flow must be routable there within its maxLatency and
    # every link already within its bandwidth, otherwise code 5. An
    # event whose t/p equals the previous state is idempotent (row
    # status 1, no version, an empty impact). Every other event routes
    # each flow before and after: a flow whose full path changes is a
    # reroute and movedDemand is the summed demand of rerouted flows; an
    # unreachable flow never reroutes (its moved is false). An event
    # passes only when every flow is reachable on the new side with its
    # new latency at most its maxLatency, no link is overloaded, the
    # exact peak increase is at most L/1000000, and
    # movedDemand/totalDemand is at most C/1000000 (integer cross
    # multiplication only, never floats). A passing event (row status 0,
    # a candidate version) carries the impact
    # [oldPeak, newPeak, delta, movedDemand, totalDemand, movedRatio,
    # flows, links]: flows in F order
    # [id, oldCost, newCost, oldLatency, newLatency, oldPath, newPath,
    # moved, pass] with a null cost/latency and [] path on an
    # unreachable side and pass reporting the new-side latency
    # compliance; links in candidate topology order
    # [from, to, bandwidth, used, utilization] for the new side,
    # peaks/movedRatio/utilization rendered as six-decimal half-up
    # strings and delta a signed six-decimal string from the exact
    # rationals. At the first failing non-idempotent event simulation
    # stops at once and the whole batch rejects: batch status 2, old/new
    # both the pre-call v, applied false, config the pre-call pack, and
    # PACK untouched in either mode.
    #
    # Once every event is a gated candidate, version/history append,
    # duplicate-resend recognition, the preview/commit difference, and
    # the single atomic replace follow op 16 exactly. For B events, K
    # distinct flow sources, F flows, V nodes, and A links the bound is
    # O(B(K(V^2+A) + FV + A)) time and O(KV + FV + A) extra space
    # besides the returned result.
    if base > v:
        fail(5)
    base_topo = history[base][1]
    base_node_set = set(base_topo["nodes"])
    for item in flows:
        if item[1] not in base_node_set or item[2] not in base_node_set:
            fail(5)
    last_e = None
    for item in events:
        e = item[0]
        if last_e is not None and e < last_e:
            fail(5)
        last_e = e
        _validate_topology(item[1], metrics=True)
        if not _is_policy(item[2]):
            fail(5)

    flow_count = len(flows)
    total_demand = 0
    for item in flows:
        total_demand += item[3]
    cur_version = base
    cur_t = history[base][1]
    cur_p = history[base][2]
    (cur_paths, cur_costs, cur_latencies, _, cur_peak,
     cur_reachable, cur_over) = _config_latency_side(
         cur_t["nodes"], cur_t["links"], flows, flow_count)
    # The batch is only defined from a feasible h[b]: every flow must be
    # routable there within its maxLatency and every link already within
    # its bandwidth.
    if not cur_reachable or cur_over:
        fail(5)
    for i, item in enumerate(flows):
        if cur_latencies[i] > item[4]:
            fail(5)

    rows = []
    suffix = []
    for event in events:
        e, new_t, new_p = event
        if new_t == cur_t and new_p == cur_p:
            rows.append([e, 1, cur_version, cur_version, []])
            continue
        if cur_version >= MAX_COST:
            fail(5)
        (new_paths, new_costs, new_latencies, new_used, new_peak,
         new_reachable, new_over) = _config_latency_side(
             new_t["nodes"], new_t["links"], flows, flow_count)
        moved = [False] * flow_count
        passed_latency = [False] * flow_count
        moved_demand = 0
        for i, item in enumerate(flows):
            np_ = new_paths[i]
            nl = new_latencies[i]
            passed_latency[i] = np_ is not None and nl <= item[4]
            op_ = cur_paths[i]
            if op_ is not None and np_ is not None and op_ != np_:
                moved[i] = True
                moved_demand += item[3]
        passed = new_reachable and not new_over and all(passed_latency)
        old_num, old_den = cur_peak
        new_num, new_den = new_peak
        if passed:
            # Exact comparison of the peak increase against L/1000000:
            # newNum/newDen - oldNum/oldDen <= L/1000000.
            delta_num = new_num * old_den - old_num * new_den
            increase_ok = (delta_num * 1000000
                           <= limit_ppm * new_den * old_den)
            if not increase_ok:
                passed = False
        if passed:
            # Exact comparison of the rerouted share against C/1000000:
            # movedDemand/totalDemand <= C/1000000.
            if moved_demand * 1000000 > moved_ppm * total_demand:
                passed = False

            impact = _config_latency_impact(
                flows, cur_costs, cur_paths, cur_latencies, cur_peak,
                new_t, new_costs, new_paths, new_latencies, new_used,
                new_peak, moved, moved_demand, total_demand,
                passed_latency)
            rows.append([e, 2, cur_version, cur_version, impact])

                    "new": v, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                    "config": pack}
        impact = _config_latency_impact(
            flows, cur_costs, cur_paths, cur_latencies, cur_peak,
            new_t, new_costs, new_paths, new_latencies, new_used,
            new_peak, moved, moved_demand, total_demand, passed_latency)
        next_version = cur_version + 1
        rows.append([e, 0, cur_version, next_version, impact])
        suffix.append([next_version, new_t, new_p])
        cur_version = next_version
        cur_t, cur_p = new_t, new_p
        cur_paths, cur_costs = new_paths, new_costs
        cur_latencies = new_latencies
        cur_peak = new_peak
    change_count = len(suffix)

    if base != v:
        # The only tolerated stale base is an exact resend: PACK must
        # already end exactly at the simulated suffix with every entry
        # equal; anything else is a version/suffix conflict.
        if change_count == 0 or v != base + change_count:
            fail(5)
        for offset, entry in enumerate(suffix, start=1):
            if history[base + offset] != entry:
                fail(5)
        return {"op": 23, "mode": mode, "status": 1, "old": base,
                "new": v, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                "config": pack}

    if change_count == 0:
        # All events idempotent at the current version: nothing to
        # append, so a commit writes nothing either.
        return {"op": 23, "mode": mode, "status": 0, "old": base,
                "new": base, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                "config": pack}
    new_pack = {"v": v + change_count, "t": cur_t, "p": cur_p,
                "h": history + suffix}
    if mode == 1:
        _write_state_atomic(pack_path, new_pack)
        applied = True
    else:
        applied = False

            "new": v + change_count, "applied": applied, "events": rows,
            "config": new_pack}


def _config_failcap_scenario(nodes, links, active_links, flows,
                             flow_count):
    # Route every flow on one failure scenario of one topology:
    # active_links is links with the scenario's single up link removed
    # (identical to links for the no-failure scenario); originally down
    # links stay down in shortest_paths. One Dijkstra per distinct
    # source with the route subcommand's lowest-cost path and
    # full-node-sequence Unicode tie break. Returns
    # (paths, costs, used, peak(Num,Den), all_reachable, any_overload)
    # exactly like _config_capacity_side; used is indexed by the full
    # links array (the failed link simply loads 0). O(K(V^2+A) + FV + A)
    # for K distinct sources, F flows, V nodes, and A links.
    node_set = set(nodes)
    cost_of = {}
    path_of = {}
    paths = [None] * flow_count
    costs = [None] * flow_count
    reachable = True
    for i, item in enumerate(flows):
        s, d = item[1], item[2]
        if s not in node_set or d not in node_set:
            reachable = False
            continue
        if s not in cost_of:
            cost_of[s], path_of[s] = shortest_paths(nodes, active_links, s)
        path = path_of[s][d]
        if path is None:
            reachable = False
            continue
        paths[i] = path
        costs[i] = cost_of[s][d]
    used = [0] * len(links)
    index_of = {}
    for index, link in enumerate(links):
        index_of[(link["from"], link["to"])] = index
    for i, item in enumerate(flows):
        if paths[i] is None:
            continue
        path = paths[i]
        demand = item[3]
        for a, c in zip(path, path[1:]):
            used[index_of[(a, c)]] += demand
    peak_num, peak_den = 0, 1
    over = False
    for index, link in enumerate(links):
        u, bw = used[index], link["bandwidth"]
        if u > bw:
            over = True
        if u * peak_den > peak_num * bw:
            peak_num, peak_den = u, bw
    return paths, costs, used, (peak_num, peak_den), reachable, over


def _config_failcap_iter(nodes, links, flows, flow_count):
    # Yield one record per scenario in scenario order: the no-failure
    # scenario first (fail_index None), then, in links order, one
    # scenario per up link with that single link treated as down. Down
    # links earn no scenario of their own (they are already absent from
    # the routed graph). Each record is the tuple returned by
    # _config_failcap_scenario prefixed by fail_index. Only one
    # scenario's routing is live at a time.
    paths, costs, used, peak, reachable, over = \
        _config_failcap_scenario(nodes, links, links, flows, flow_count)
    yield None, paths, costs, used, peak, reachable, over
    for fail_index, link in enumerate(links):
        if not link["up"]:
            continue
        active_links = [other for j, other in enumerate(links)
                        if j != fail_index]
        paths, costs, used, peak, reachable, over = \
            _config_failcap_scenario(nodes, links, active_links, flows,
                                     flow_count)
        yield fail_index, paths, costs, used, peak, reachable, over


def _config_failcap_assess(nodes, links, flows, flow_count, render):
    # Walk one side's scenarios in order, tracking only the running
    # worst (the first strict maximum wins, records being visited in
    # tie-break order). When render is true each new-side scenario is
    # emitted straight into the returned rows as
    # [failedLink, peak, pass, flows, links] - those rows are the
    # result, not working space; the old side renders nothing. Returns
    # (worst_index, worst_num, worst_den, all_reachable, no_over, rows)
    # with the no-failure tag represented by worst_index None. Extra
    # space is just the one live scenario: O(KV + FV + A).
    worst_index = None
    worst_num, worst_den = 0, 1
    all_reachable = True
    no_over = True
    rows = []
    for rec in _config_failcap_iter(nodes, links, flows, flow_count):
        (fail_index, paths, costs, used, peak,
         reachable, over) = rec
        num, den = peak
        if num * worst_den > worst_num * den:
            worst_index, worst_num, worst_den = fail_index, num, den
        if not reachable:
            all_reachable = False
        if over:
            no_over = False
        if render:
            flow_rows = [[item[0], costs[i],
                          [] if paths[i] is None else paths[i]]
                         for i, item in enumerate(flows)]
            link_rows = []
            for index, link in enumerate(links):
                u = used[index]
                link_rows.append([link["from"], link["to"],
                                  link["bandwidth"], u,
                                  _config_capacity_six(u,
                                                       link["bandwidth"])])
            tag = None if fail_index is None else \
                [links[fail_index]["from"], links[fail_index]["to"]]
            rows.append([tag, _config_capacity_six(num, den),
                         reachable and not over, flow_rows, link_rows])
    return (worst_index, worst_num, worst_den, all_reachable, no_over,
            rows)


def _config_failcap_tag(links, fail_index):
    # A worst tag: null for the no-failure scenario, else the failed
    # link's [from, to].
    if fail_index is None:
        return None
    link = links[fail_index]
    return [link["from"], link["to"]]


def _config_failcap_impact(old_links, old_index, old_num, old_den,

    # Build the [oldWorst, newWorst, delta, scenarios] impact row from

    # for the no-failure scenario else [from, to], peak a six-decimal

            _config_capacity_delta_six(new_num, new_den, old_num, old_den),
            scenario_rows]

def _config_latency_side(nodes, links, flows, flow_count):
    # Route every flow on one topology for the latency gate (config op
    # 23), exactly like _config_capacity_side - the route subcommand's
    # lowest-cost path over up links with the full-node-sequence Unicode
    # tie break, one Dijkstra per distinct source - and additionally sum
    # each chosen path's link latencies. A flow item is
    # [id, source, destination, demand, maxLatency]; the per-flow
    # maxLatency is used by the caller, not here. Returns
    # (paths, costs, latencies, used, peak(Num,Den), all_reachable,
    # any_overload) with a None slot for paths/costs/latencies on an
    # unreachable side. A reachable path whose latency sum exceeds
    # MAX_TIME fails code 5. O(K(V^2 + A) + FV + A) for K distinct
    # sources, F flows, V nodes, and A links.
    node_set = set(nodes)
    cost_of = {}
    path_of = {}
    lat_of = {}
    for link in links:
        lat_of[(link["from"], link["to"])] = link["latency"]
    paths = [None] * flow_count
    costs = [None] * flow_count
    latencies = [None] * flow_count
    reachable = True
    for i, item in enumerate(flows):
        s, d = item[1], item[2]
        if s not in node_set or d not in node_set:
            reachable = False
            continue
        if s not in cost_of:
            cost_of[s], path_of[s] = shortest_paths(nodes, links, s)
        path = path_of[s][d]
        if path is None:
            reachable = False
            continue
        latency = 0
        for a, c in zip(path, path[1:]):
            latency += lat_of[(a, c)]
            if latency > MAX_TIME:
                fail(5)
        paths[i] = path
        costs[i] = cost_of[s][d]
        latencies[i] = latency
    used = [0] * len(links)
    index_of = {}
    for index, link in enumerate(links):
        index_of[(link["from"], link["to"])] = index
    for i, item in enumerate(flows):
        if paths[i] is None:
            continue
        path = paths[i]
        demand = item[3]
        for a, c in zip(path, path[1:]):
            used[index_of[(a, c)]] += demand
    peak_num, peak_den = 0, 1
    over = False
    for index, link in enumerate(links):
        u, bw = used[index], link["bandwidth"]
        if u > bw:
            over = True
        if u * peak_den > peak_num * bw:
            peak_num, peak_den = u, bw
    return (paths, costs, latencies, used, (peak_num, peak_den),
            reachable, over)


def _config_latency_impact(flows, old_costs, old_paths, old_latencies,
                           old_peak, new_topo, new_costs, new_paths,
                           new_latencies, new_used, new_peak, moved,
                           moved_demand, total_demand, passed_latency):
    # Build the [oldPeak, newPeak, delta, movedDemand, totalDemand,
    # movedRatio, flows, links] impact row for a latency-gated event,
    # carrying op 22's envelope with old/new latency and a per-flow pass
    # flag added. Flow rows follow F order as
    # [id, oldCost, newCost, oldLatency, newLatency, oldPath, newPath,
    # moved, pass] with moved a plain boolean marking a path change
    # between two reachable sides and pass a plain boolean marking the
    # new-side latency at most the flow's maxLatency (false on an
    # unreachable new side); an unreachable side is a null cost, a null
    # latency, and []. Link rows follow the new (candidate) topology's
    # link order, each [from, to, bandwidth, used, utilization].
    old_num, old_den = old_peak
    new_num, new_den = new_peak
    flow_rows = []
    for i, item in enumerate(flows):
        fid = item[0]
        oc = old_costs[i]
        ol = old_latencies[i]
        op_ = old_paths[i]
        nc = new_costs[i]
        nl = new_latencies[i]
        np_ = new_paths[i]
        flow_rows.append([fid, oc, nc, ol, nl,
                          [] if op_ is None else op_,
                          [] if np_ is None else np_,
                          bool(moved[i]), bool(passed_latency[i])])
    link_rows = []
    for index, link in enumerate(new_topo["links"]):
        u = new_used[index]
        bw = link["bandwidth"]
        link_rows.append([link["from"], link["to"], bw, u,
                          _config_capacity_six(u, bw)])
    return [_config_capacity_six(old_num, old_den),
            _config_capacity_six(new_num, new_den),
            _config_capacity_delta_six(new_num, new_den, old_num, old_den),
            moved_demand, total_demand,
            _config_capacity_six(moved_demand, total_demand),
            flow_rows, link_rows]

def _state_payload(state):
    # Canonical on-disk form: top-level key order v,p,h, compact
    # separators, non-ASCII UTF-8, integers in decimal, one trailing LF.
    text = json.dumps(state, ensure_ascii=False,
                      separators=(",", ":")) + "\n"
    return text.encode("utf-8")


def _write_state_atomic(path, state):
    # Replace the state file atomically: serialize, then exclusively
    # create a unique sibling temp file with an incrementing suffix (a
    # collision only retries under the next name), flush+fsync it,
    # os.replace it over the destination, then fsync the directory.
    # Any failure removes only the temp file this call acquired and
    # leaves the destination byte-for-byte untouched.
    payload = _state_payload(state)
    directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(path))
    suffix = 0
    while True:
        tmp_path = path + ".tmp." + str(suffix)
        try:
            fd = os.open(tmp_path,
                         os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL, 0o666)
        except FileExistsError:
            suffix += 1
            continue
        except OSError:
            fail(3)
        break
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as f:
            f.write(payload)
            f.flush()
            os.fsync(f.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, path)
        try:
            dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
            try:
                os.fsync(dir_fd)
            finally:

我已经充分理解结构。现在需要弄清楚一个关键点：op 27 的语义与 op 26 的差别。

**op 27 语义梳理（[27,m,b,E,F,S,L]）：**
- m, b, E, S, L 与 op 26 相同
- F 每项是 `[id, source, destination, demand, maxLatency]`（5 字段，同 op 23 的 F），maxLatency 为 0..MAX_COST 的非布尔整数（注意：**不是 0..MAX_TIME**！spec 明确说 "maxLatency 是 0 至 MAX_COST 的非布尔整数"）
- 验证从 h[b] 开始，按 E 顺序处理
- 每事件依次评估无故障场景和 S 中各场景
- 场景停用指定节点、关联链路及指定有向链路；候选删除的引用对象不可用（与 op 26 相同）
- 流在可用链路中选最低代价路径，平局按完整节点序列 Unicode 码点
- **时延 = 路径各链路 latency 的整数和**
- 候选仅在以下条件全部满足时通过：
  1. 所有场景的流均可达
  2. 链路不超 bandwidth
  3. **流时延不超过自身 maxLatency**
  4. 新旧最坏峰值利用率精确增量 ≤ L/1000000，整数交叉相乘
- 相同配置事件幂等，不新增版本，impact 为空（[]）
- 结果键序：op、mode、status、old、new、applied、events、config
- impact = [oldWorst, newWorst, delta, scenarios]
  - worst = [scenarioId, peak]（无故障 scenarioId 为 null）
  - scenarios 按既定次序：[scenarioId, peak, pass, flows, links]
  - flows 按 F 顺序：**[id, cost, latency, maxLatency, path, pass]**
  - links 按拓扑顺序：[from, to, bandwidth, used, utilization]
  - 不可达流为 [id, null, null, maxLatency, [], false]
- 基线侧（h[b]）任一场景不可达、超载或**超时**（即流时延 > maxLatency？）→ code 5
- 输入形状/类型/范围/引用/版本连续性/MAX_TIME 运算有误 → 5
- JSON 错 4，文件错 3
- 首个未通过事件 status 2，停止，保留调用前配置
- 全部通过：预览无写入；提交最多原子替换 PACK 一次；失败不留临时文件；重复提交不改写
- 上界 O(B(S+1)(K(V²+A)+FV+A)) 时间，O(KV+FV+A) 空间

**关于 "超时" 的理解：** "基线侧任一场景不可达、超载或超时" → code 5。超时指什么？对照 op 23：reachable path whose latency sum exceeds MAX_TIME is code 5；以及 h[b] 侧流 latency > maxLatency 也是 code 5。对 op 27，"超时" 应该有两层含义：
1. 时延整数和超过 MAX_TIME（运算溢出）→ 这属于 "MAX_TIME 运算有误" → code 5
2. 基线侧流时延 > maxLatency（"基线侧…超时"）→ code 5

spec 原文："基线侧任一场景不可达、超载或超时，或输入形状、类型、范围、引用、版本连续性、MAX_TIME 运算有误，均返回参数类退出码 5"。所以基线侧的 "超时" = 流时延超过自身 maxLatency。新侧超时只是事件不通过（status 2）。而 MAX_TIME 运算有误（latency 求和超过 MAX_TIME）是任何侧都 code 5（与 op 23 一致）。

注意 maxLatency 范围是 0..MAX_COST（不是 MAX_TIME）。链路 latency 的范围呢？需要看 _validate_topology。链路 latency 可能在 0..MAX_TIME？求latency和时参照 op 23：超过 MAX_TIME 则 fail(5)。

**场景 pass 标记：**
- op 26: scenario row 的 pass = `reachable and not over`
- op 27: pass 应包括时延：`reachable and not over and all flows latency <= maxLatency`。因为候选通过条件是每个场景的所有流可达、不超载、时延不超 maxLatency。场景级 pass 标记自然表示该场景全部满足。

**流级 pass：** [id, cost, latency, maxLatency, path, pass] —— 可达且 latency ≤ maxLatency 时 true；不可达 [id,null,null,maxLatency,[],false]。可达但超时 → pass false，cost/latency/path 有值。

**worst 峰值的选择：** 与 op 26 相同 —— 各场景 peak（最大 used/bandwidth），选最大者，平局无故障优先、再按 S 次序。时延门禁不影响 worst 选择。

**worst 是否应只在 "通过的场景" 中选？** op 26 的实现：`_config_compound_assess` 无论场景是否通过都追踪 worst（对所有场景跑，num*worst_den > ... 即更新）。op 27 沿用：worst 是所有场景里的最大峰值，即便某场景时延不达标。delta 比较照常用。这与 op 26 一致。

**delta 判定：** 与 op 26 相同的交叉相乘。

**基线校验：** h[b] 每个场景（含无故障）：所有流可达、无超载、且每个流 latency ≤ maxLatency → 否则 code 5。还有 latency 求和 > MAX_TIME → fail(5)（在 side 路由内）。

**新侧：** 所有场景：所有流可达、无超载、每个流 latency ≤ maxLatency，再加上 worst-peak 增量 ≤ L/1e6 → 事件通过。

现在设计实现。我将镜像 op 26 的结构，写一组 op 27 函数：

1. `_config_clatency_scenario(nodes, links, active_links, flows, flow_count)` —— 类似 `_config_failcap_scenario` 但额外返回 latencies 数组（整数和，超 MAX_TIME fail(5)）。
   实际上可以直接仿照 `_config_latency_side`（它已返回 paths, costs, latencies, used, peak, reachable, over），但签名是 (nodes, links, flows, count)，对故障场景需要 active_links。`_config_failcap_scenario` 的 active_links 模式正好。我写一个合并版：`_config_clatency_scenario(nodes, links, active_links, flows, flow_count)` 返回 `(paths, costs, latencies, used, peak, reachable, over)`。

2. `_config_clatency_iter(nodes, links, flows, flow_count, prepared)` —— 镜像 `_config_compound_iter`，产出 `(sid, paths, costs, latencies, used, peak, reachable, over)`。

3. `_config_clatency_assess(nodes, links, flows, flow_count, prepared, render)` —— 镜像 `_config_compound_assess`，额外：
   - 追踪 all_latency_ok（每流 latency ≤ item[4]）
   - 渲染 flow_rows = [id, cost, latency, maxLatency, path, pass]
   - scenario pass = reachable and not over and latency_ok（该场景内所有流）
   返回 `(worst_sid, worst_num, worst_den, all_reachable, no_over, all_latency_ok, rows)`。

4. `_config_clatency_impact(...)` —— 镜像 `_config_compound_impact`，签名相同（scenario_rows 已含时延列）。

5. `_config_clatency_gate_batch(...)` —— 镜像 `_config_compound_gate_batch`：
   - F 为 5 字段
   - 初始 assess(render=False) 检查 reachable/no_over/**latency_ok**，否则 fail(5)
   - 每事件 idempotent 检查
   - render=True assess 新侧
   - passed = new_reachable and new_no_over and new_latency_ok，再加交叉相乘
   - 结果键 op 27
   - 幂等/重发/原子写完全一致

6. 入口分派：
   - 新增 `elif kind == 27:` 形状校验：len 7；m/b/E 同 26；F 每项 len==5，maxLatency type int 且 0 <= <= MAX_COST（注意 bool 排除：`type(x) is int`）；S 同 26；L 同 26。
   - `elif kind == 27: result = _config_clatency_gate_batch(...)`。

等等——关于 maxLatency 范围。spec："maxLatency 是 0 至 MAX_COST 的非布尔整数"。所以入口校验 `0 <= max_latency <= MAX_COST`。而 op 23 是 0..MAX_TIME。这里明确是 MAX_COST。

关于 latency 求和与 MAX_TIME：路径 latency 为 "路径各链路 latency 的整数和"。如果和 > MAX_TIME，按 "MAX_TIME 运算有误" code 5（参照 op 23 的处理：边加边判 `if latency > MAX_TIME: fail(5)`）。链路 latency 本身的范围由 _validate_topology 保证。让我确认一下 topology 校验中 latency 的范围。

另外注意：基线 h[b] 侧如果 latency 超 maxLatency → code 5（"超时"）。这与 op 23 相同处理。

**flow pass 定义** —— 可达且 latency ≤ maxLatency。不可达 false。

**scenario pass** —— 全部流可达（等价于每流可达）、无超载、每流时延达标。

def _config_capacity_six(num, den):
    # num/den rounded half up to six decimals like _format_peak.
    scaled = (2 * num * 1000000 + den) // (2 * den)
    return "%d.%06d" % (scaled // 1000000, scaled % 1000000)


def _config_capacity_delta_six(new_num, new_den, old_num, old_den):
    # Signed six-decimal rendering of newPeak - oldPeak, rounded half up
    # from the exact rational difference (not a subtraction of rounded
    # strings); an exact zero is "0.000000". All arithmetic is integer.
    delta_num = new_num * old_den - old_num * new_den
    delta_den = new_den * old_den
    if delta_num == 0:
        return "0.000000"
    sign = "-" if delta_num < 0 else "+"
    scaled = (2 * abs(delta_num) * 1000000 + delta_den) // (2 * delta_den)
    body = "%d.%06d" % (scaled // 1000000, scaled % 1000000)
    return sign + body


def _config_capacity_side(nodes, links, flows, flow_count):
    # Route every flow on one topology: the route subcommand's lowest-
    # cost path over up links with the full-node-sequence Unicode tie
    # break, one Dijkstra per distinct source. Returns
    # (paths, costs, used, peak(Num,Den), all_reachable, any_overload).

def _config_clatency_scenario(nodes, links, active_links, flows,
                              flow_count):
    # Route every flow on one failure scenario of one topology for the
    # compound-failure latency gate (config op 27): exactly like
    # _config_failcap_scenario - the route subcommand's lowest-cost path
    # over up links with the full-node-sequence Unicode tie break, one
    # Dijkstra per distinct source, used indexed by the full links array
    # (a failed link simply loads 0) - and additionally sum each chosen
    # path's link latencies as an integer. A flow item is
    # [id, source, destination, demand, maxLatency]; the per-flow
    # maxLatency is used by the caller, not here. Returns
    # (paths, costs, latencies, used, peak(Num,Den), all_reachable,
    # any_overload) with a None slot for paths/costs/latencies on an
    # unreachable side. A reachable path whose latency sum exceeds
    # MAX_TIME fails code 5. O(K(V^2+A) + FV + A) for K distinct
    # sources, F flows, V nodes, and A links.
    node_set = set(nodes)
    cost_of = {}
    path_of = {}
    lat_of = {}
    for link in links:
        lat_of[(link["from"], link["to"])] = link["latency"]
    paths = [None] * flow_count
    costs = [None] * flow_count
    latencies = [None] * flow_count
    reachable = True
    for i, item in enumerate(flows):
        s, d = item[1], item[2]
        if s not in node_set or d not in node_set:
            reachable = False
            continue
        if s not in cost_of:
            cost_of[s], path_of[s] = shortest_paths(nodes, active_links, s)
        path = path_of[s][d]
        if path is None:
            reachable = False
            continue
        latency = 0
        for a, c in zip(path, path[1:]):
            latency += lat_of[(a, c)]
            if latency > MAX_TIME:
                fail(5)
        paths[i] = path
        costs[i] = cost_of[s][d]
        latencies[i] = latency
    used = [0] * len(links)
    index_of = {}
    for index, link in enumerate(links):
        index_of[(link["from"], link["to"])] = index
    for i, item in enumerate(flows):
        if paths[i] is None:
            continue
        path = paths[i]
        demand = item[3]
        for a, c in zip(path, path[1:]):
            used[index_of[(a, c)]] += demand
    peak_num, peak_den = 0, 1
    over = False
    for index, link in enumerate(links):
        u, bw = used[index], link["bandwidth"]
        if u > bw:
            over = True
        if u * peak_den > peak_num * bw:
            peak_num, peak_den = u, bw
    return (paths, costs, latencies, used, (peak_num, peak_den),
            reachable, over)

    # Yield one record per compound-failure scenario in scenario order:
    # the no-failure scenario first (sid None), then one record per
    # prepared scenario in S order, exactly like _config_compound_iter
    # but carrying each path's integer latency sum. Each record is the
    # tuple returned by _config_clatency_scenario prefixed by the
    # scenario id (None for the no-failure scenario). Only one
    # scenario's routing is live at a time.
    paths, costs, latencies, used, peak, reachable, over = \
        _config_clatency_scenario(nodes, links, links, flows, flow_count)
    yield None, paths, costs, latencies, used, peak, reachable, over
    for sid, fail_node_set, explicit_pairs in prepared:
        active_nodes = [node for node in nodes
                        if node not in fail_node_set]
        active_links = [link for link in links
                        if link["from"] not in fail_node_set
                        and link["to"] not in fail_node_set
                        and (link["from"], link["to"]) not in
                        explicit_pairs]
        paths, costs, latencies, used, peak, reachable, over = \
            _config_clatency_scenario(active_nodes, links, active_links,
                                      flows, flow_count)
        yield sid, paths, costs, latencies, used, peak, reachable, over


def _config_clatency_assess(nodes, links, flows, flow_count, prepared,
                            render):
    # Walk one side's compound-failure scenarios in order for op 27,
    # tracking only the running worst (the first strict maximum wins,
    # records being visited in tie-break order: no-failure then S
    # order). A scenario fails the side when any flow is unreachable,
    # any link is overloaded, or any reachable flow's integer latency
    # sum exceeds its own maxLatency. When render is true each new-side
    # scenario is emitted straight into the returned rows as
    # [scenarioId, peak, pass, flows, links] - those rows are the
    # result, not working space; the old side renders nothing. Flow
    # rows follow F order as [id, cost, latency, maxLatency, path] with
    # an unreachable flow [id, null, null, maxLatency, [], false]; link
    # rows follow topology order as
    # [from, to, bandwidth, used, utilization]. Returns
    # (worst_sid, worst_num, worst_den, all_reachable, no_over,
    # latency_ok, rows) with the no-failure tag represented by
    # worst_sid None. Extra space is just the one live scenario:
    # O(KV + FV + A).
    worst_sid = None
    worst_num, worst_den = 0, 1
    all_reachable = True
    no_over = True
    latency_ok = True
    rows = []
    for rec in _config_clatency_iter(nodes, links, flows, flow_count,
                                     prepared):
        (sid, paths, costs, latencies, used, peak,
         reachable, over) = rec
        num, den = peak
        if num * worst_den > worst_num * den:
            worst_sid, worst_num, worst_den = sid, num, den
        scenario_latency_ok = True
        for i, item in enumerate(flows):
            if paths[i] is not None and latencies[i] > item[4]:
                scenario_latency_ok = False
        if not reachable:
            all_reachable = False
        if over:
            no_over = False
        if not scenario_latency_ok:
            latency_ok = False
        if render:
            flow_rows = []
            for i, item in enumerate(flows):
                if paths[i] is None:
                    flow_rows.append([item[0], None, None, item[4], [],
                                      False])
                else:
                    flow_rows.append([item[0], costs[i], latencies[i],
                                      item[4], paths[i],
                                      scenario_latency_ok
                                      if False else
                                      (latencies[i] <= item[4])])
            link_rows = []
            for index, link in enumerate(links):
                u = used[index]
                link_rows.append([link["from"], link["to"],
                                  link["bandwidth"], u,
                                  _config_capacity_six(u,
                                                       link["bandwidth"])])
            rows.append([sid, _config_capacity_six(num, den),
                         reachable and not over and scenario_latency_ok,
                         flow_rows, link_rows])
    return (worst_sid, worst_num, worst_den, all_reachable, no_over,
            latency_ok, rows)


def _config_clatency_gate_batch(pack_path, pack, v, history, mode, base,
                                events, flows, limit_ppm, scenario_specs):
    # Batched hotload with a per-event compound-failure latency gate
    # (config op 27): [27, m, b, E, F, S, L]. m, b, E, the named
    # scenarios S, and L (the worst-utilization-increase cap in parts
    # per million) carry op 26's exact semantics; F is a non-empty
    # array of [id, source, destination, demand, maxLatency] flows
    # shaped exactly like op 23's, with maxLatency a non-boolean
    # integer in 0..MAX_COST.
    #
    # Every input validates first (shapes in the command entry; the h[b]
    # reference/endpoint/scenario checks, clocks, and event t/p here),
    # then simulation walks from h[b] in E order. Failure objects an
    # earlier candidate deleted are unavailable on that later side and
    # simply drop out of its scenario routing. For each compared side
    # the flows are routed in scenario order: the no-failure scenario
    # first and then each S scenario in order, with its failed nodes,
    # their associated links, and its explicit failure links removed.
    # A scenario routes each flow on the lowest-cost available path
    # with shortest_paths' full-node-sequence Unicode tie break; the
    # flow's latency is the integer sum of its path's link latencies;
    # a link's used is the summed demand of the flows traversing it and
    # the scenario peak is the exact maximum used/bandwidth; the worst
    # scenario is the largest peak, an equal peak broken by no-failure
    # then S order. Any unreachable flow, overloaded link, or
    # beyond-maxLatency flow in an old-side scenario - including every
    # scenario at h[b] - is code 5, as is a reachable path whose
    # latency sum exceeds MAX_TIME.
    #
    # An event whose t/p equals the previous state is idempotent (row
    # status 1, no version, an empty impact). Every other event passes
    # only when every new-side scenario has every flow reachable
    # within its own maxLatency and no overloaded link, and the exact
    # worst-peak increase is at most L/1000000 (integer cross
    # multiplication only, never floats). A passing event (row status
    # 0, a candidate version) and the first failing event alike carry
    # the impact [oldWorst, newWorst, delta, scenarios] with a worst
    # [scenarioId, peak] (scenarioId null for no failure else the
    # scenario id string) and scenarios listing only the new side as
    # [scenarioId, peak, pass, flows, links]; flows are
    # [id, cost, latency, maxLatency, path, pass]
    # ([id, null, null, maxLatency, [], false] when unreachable) and
    # links [from, to, bandwidth, used, utilization] in topology
    # order, the ratios six-decimal half-up strings and delta signed.
    # At the first failing event simulation stops at once and the
    # whole batch rejects: batch status 2, old/new both the pre-call v,
    # applied false, config the pre-call pack, and PACK untouched in
    # either mode.
    #
    # Once every event is a gated candidate, version/history append,
    # duplicate-resend recognition, the preview/commit difference, and
    # the single atomic replace follow op 16 exactly. For B events, S
    # scenarios, K distinct flow sources, F flows, V nodes, and A links
    # the bound is O(B(S+1)(K(V^2+A) + FV + A)) time and
    # O(KV + FV + A) extra space besides the returned result.
    if base > v:
        fail(5)
    base_topo = history[base][1]
    base_node_set = set(base_topo["nodes"])
    for item in flows:
        if item[1] not in base_node_set or item[2] not in base_node_set:
            fail(5)
    prepared = _config_compound_prepare(base_topo["nodes"],
                                        base_topo["links"], flows,
                                        scenario_specs)
    last_e = None
    for item in events:
        e = item[0]
        if last_e is not None and e < last_e:
            fail(5)
        last_e = e
        _validate_topology(item[1], metrics=True)
        if not _is_policy(item[2]):
            fail(5)

    flow_count = len(flows)
    cur_version = base
    cur_t = history[base][1]
    cur_p = history[base][2]
    (cur_worst_sid, cur_worst_num, cur_worst_den,
     cur_reachable, cur_no_over, cur_latency_ok, _) = \
        _config_clatency_assess(cur_t["nodes"], cur_t["links"], flows,
                                flow_count, prepared, False)
    # The batch is only defined from a failure-feasible h[b]: every
    # flow must be routable in every scenario within its maxLatency and
    # every link within its bandwidth there.
    if not cur_reachable or not cur_no_over or not cur_latency_ok:
        fail(5)

    rows = []
    suffix = []
    for event in events:
        e, new_t, new_p = event
        if new_t == cur_t and new_p == cur_p:
            rows.append([e, 1, cur_version, cur_version, []])
            continue
        if cur_version >= MAX_COST:
            fail(5)
        (new_worst_sid, new_worst_num, new_worst_den,
         new_reachable, new_no_over, new_latency_ok, scenario_rows) = \
            _config_clatency_assess(new_t["nodes"], new_t["links"],
                                    flows, flow_count, prepared, True)
        passed = (new_reachable and new_no_over and new_latency_ok)
        if passed:
            # Exact comparison of the worst-peak increase against
            # L/1000000: newWorst - oldWorst <= L/1000000.
            delta_num = new_worst_num * cur_worst_den \
                - cur_worst_num * new_worst_den
            increase_ok = (delta_num * 1000000
                           <= limit_ppm * new_worst_den * cur_worst_den)
            if not increase_ok:
                passed = False
        impact = _config_compound_impact(
            cur_worst_sid, cur_worst_num, cur_worst_den,
            new_worst_sid, new_worst_num, new_worst_den, scenario_rows)
        if not passed:
            rows.append([e, 2, cur_version, cur_version, impact])
            return {"op": 27, "mode": mode, "status": 2, "old": v,
                    "new": v, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                    "config": pack}
        next_version = cur_version + 1
        rows.append([e, 0, cur_version, next_version, impact])
        suffix.append([next_version, new_t, new_p])
        cur_version = next_version
        cur_t, cur_p = new_t, new_p
        cur_worst_sid = new_worst_sid
        cur_worst_num, cur_worst_den = new_worst_num, new_worst_den
    change_count = len(suffix)

    if base != v:
        # The only tolerated stale base is an exact resend: PACK must
        # already end exactly at the simulated suffix with every entry
        # equal; anything else is a version/suffix conflict.
        if change_count == 0 or v != base + change_count:
            fail(5)
        for offset, entry in enumerate(suffix, start=1):
            if history[base + offset] != entry:
                fail(5)
        return {"op": 27, "mode": mode, "status": 1, "old": base,
                "new": v, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                "config": pack}

    if change_count == 0:
        # All events idempotent at the current version: nothing to
        # append, so a commit writes nothing either.
        return {"op": 27, "mode": mode, "status": 0, "old": base,
                "new": base, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                "config": pack}
    new_pack = {"v": v + change_count, "t": cur_t, "p": cur_p,
                "h": history + suffix}
    if mode == 1:
        _write_state_atomic(pack_path, new_pack)
        applied = True
    else:
        applied = False
    return {"op": 27, "mode": mode, "status": 0, "old": base,
            "new": v + change_count, "applied": applied, "events": rows,
            "config": new_pack}

def _config_clatency_gate_batch(pack_path, pack, v, history, mode, base,
                                events, flows, limit_ppm, scenario_specs):
    # Batched hotload with a per-event compound-failure latency gate
    # (config op 27): [27, m, b, E, F, S, L]. m, b, E, the named
    # scenarios S, and L (the worst-utilization-increase cap in parts
    # per million) carry op 26's exact semantics; F is a non-empty
    # array of [id, source, destination, demand, maxLatency] flows
    # shaped exactly like op 23's, with maxLatency a non-boolean
    # integer in 0..MAX_COST.
    #
    # Every input validates first (shapes in the command entry; the h[b]
    # reference/endpoint/scenario checks, clocks, and event t/p here),
    # then simulation walks from h[b] in E order. Failure objects an
    # earlier candidate deleted are unavailable on that later side and
    # simply drop out of its scenario routing. For each compared side
    # the flows are routed in scenario order: the no-failure scenario
    # first and then each S scenario in order, with its failed nodes,
    # their associated links, and its explicit failure links removed.
    # A scenario routes each flow on the lowest-cost available path
    # with shortest_paths' full-node-sequence Unicode tie break; the
    # flow's latency is the integer sum of its path's link latencies;
    # a link's used is the summed demand of the flows traversing it and
    # the scenario peak is the exact maximum used/bandwidth; the worst
    # scenario is the largest peak, an equal peak broken by no-failure
    # then S order. Any unreachable flow, overloaded link, or
    # beyond-maxLatency flow in an old-side scenario - including every
    # scenario at h[b] - is code 5, as is a reachable path whose
    # latency sum exceeds MAX_TIME.
    #
    # An event whose t/p equals the previous state is idempotent (row
    # status 1, no version, an empty impact). Every other event passes
    # only when every new-side scenario has every flow reachable
    # within its own maxLatency and no overloaded link, and the exact
    # worst-peak increase is at most L/1000000 (integer cross
    # multiplication only, never floats). A passing event (row status
    # 0, a candidate version) and the first failing event alike carry
    # the impact [oldWorst, newWorst, delta, scenarios] with a worst
    # [scenarioId, peak] (scenarioId null for no failure else the
    # scenario id string) and scenarios listing only the new side as
    # [scenarioId, peak, pass, flows, links]; flows are
    # [id, cost, latency, maxLatency, path, pass]
    # ([id, null, null, maxLatency, [], false] when unreachable) and
    # links [from, to, bandwidth, used, utilization] in topology
    # order, the ratios six-decimal half-up strings and delta signed.
    # At the first failing event simulation stops at once and the
    # whole batch rejects: batch status 2, old/new both the pre-call v,
    # applied false, config the pre-call pack, and PACK untouched in
    # either mode.
    #
    # Once every event is a gated candidate, version/history append,
    # duplicate-resend recognition, the preview/commit difference, and
    # the single atomic replace follow op 16 exactly. For B events, S
    # scenarios, K distinct flow sources, F flows, V nodes, and A links
    # the bound is O(B(S+1)(K(V^2+A) + FV + A)) time and
    # O(KV + FV + A) extra space besides the returned result.
    if base > v:
        fail(5)
    base_topo = history[base][1]
    base_node_set = set(base_topo["nodes"])
    for item in flows:
        if item[1] not in base_node_set or item[2] not in base_node_set:
            fail(5)
    prepared = _config_compound_prepare(base_topo["nodes"],
                                        base_topo["links"], flows,
                                        scenario_specs)
    last_e = None
    for item in events:
        e = item[0]
        if last_e is not None and e < last_e:
            fail(5)
        last_e = e
        _validate_topology(item[1], metrics=True)
        if not _is_policy(item[2]):
            fail(5)

    flow_count = len(flows)
    cur_version = base
    cur_t = history[base][1]
    cur_p = history[base][2]
    (cur_worst_sid, cur_worst_num, cur_worst_den,
     cur_reachable, cur_no_over, cur_latency_ok, _) = \
        _config_clatency_assess(cur_t["nodes"], cur_t["links"], flows,
                                flow_count, prepared, False)
    # The batch is only defined from a failure-feasible h[b]: every
    # flow must be routable in every scenario within its maxLatency and
    # every link within its bandwidth there.
    if not cur_reachable or not cur_no_over or not cur_latency_ok:
        fail(5)

    rows = []
    suffix = []
    for event in events:
        e, new_t, new_p = event
        if new_t == cur_t and new_p == cur_p:
            rows.append([e, 1, cur_version, cur_version, []])
            continue
        if cur_version >= MAX_COST:
            fail(5)
        (new_worst_sid, new_worst_num, new_worst_den,
         new_reachable, new_no_over, new_latency_ok, scenario_rows) = \
            _config_clatency_assess(new_t["nodes"], new_t["links"],
                                    flows, flow_count, prepared, True)
        passed = (new_reachable and new_no_over and new_latency_ok)
        if passed:
            # Exact comparison of the worst-peak increase against
            # L/1000000: newWorst - oldWorst <= L/1000000.
            delta_num = new_worst_num * cur_worst_den \
                - cur_worst_num * new_worst_den
            increase_ok = (delta_num * 1000000
                           <= limit_ppm * new_worst_den * cur_worst_den)
            if not increase_ok:
                passed = False
        impact = _config_compound_impact(
            cur_worst_sid, cur_worst_num, cur_worst_den,
            new_worst_sid, new_worst_num, new_worst_den, scenario_rows)
        if not passed:
            rows.append([e, 2, cur_version, cur_version, impact])
            return {"op": 27, "mode": mode, "status": 2, "old": v,
                    "new": v, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                    "config": pack}
        next_version = cur_version + 1
        rows.append([e, 0, cur_version, next_version, impact])
        suffix.append([next_version, new_t, new_p])
        cur_version = next_version
        cur_t, cur_p = new_t, new_p
        cur_worst_sid = new_worst_sid
        cur_worst_num, cur_worst_den = new_worst_num, new_worst_den
    change_count = len(suffix)

    if base != v:
        # The only tolerated stale base is an exact resend: PACK must
        # already end exactly at the simulated suffix with every entry
        # equal; anything else is a version/suffix conflict.
        if change_count == 0 or v != base + change_count:
            fail(5)
        for offset, entry in enumerate(suffix, start=1):
            if history[base + offset] != entry:
                fail(5)
        return {"op": 27, "mode": mode, "status": 1, "old": base,
                "new": v, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                "config": pack}

    if change_count == 0:
        # All events idempotent at the current version: nothing to
        # append, so a commit writes nothing either.
        return {"op": 27, "mode": mode, "status": 0, "old": base,
                "new": base, "applied": False, "events": rows,
                "config": pack}
    new_pack = {"v": v + change_count, "t": cur_t, "p": cur_p,
                "h": history + suffix}
    if mode == 1:
        _write_state_atomic(pack_path, new_pack)
        applied = True
    else:
        applied = False
    return {"op": 27, "mode": mode, "status": 0, "old": base,
            "new": v + change_count, "applied": applied, "events": rows,
            "config": new_pack}

import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
RELAY = os.path.join(HERE, "relay.py")

P = [0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0]


def link(frm, to, cost=1, bw=100, lat=10, up=True):
    return {"from": frm, "to": to, "cost": cost, "bandwidth": bw,
            "latency": lat, "up": up}


def base_topo():
    # n0 -> n1 -> n3 -> n4 and n0 -> n2 -> n3; both n0->n4 paths cost
    # 3, the n1 path winning the full-node-sequence Unicode tie break.
    return {"nodes": ["n0", "n1", "n2", "n3", "n4"],
            "links": [link("n0", "n1", lat=10),
                      link("n1", "n3", lat=10),
                      link("n0", "n2", lat=50),
                      link("n2", "n3", lat=50),
                      link("n3", "n4", lat=10)]}


def pack(topo=None, v=0, history=None):
    topo = topo or base_topo()
    h = history if history is not None else [[0, topo, P]]
    return {"v": v, "t": topo, "p": P, "h": h}


SCENARIOS = [["x", ["n1"], []], ["z", [], [["n0", "n1"]]]]


def flow(fid="f1", src="n0", dst="n4", demand=40, mlat=110):
    return [fid, src, dst, demand, mlat]


def run(pack_obj, op, expect_rc=0):
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
        pp = os.path.join(d, "pack.json")
        with open(pp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(pack_obj, f)
        r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, RELAY, "config", pp,
                            json.dumps(op)], capture_output=True, text=True)
        if r.returncode != expect_rc:
            raise AssertionError("rc=%s stderr=%s stdout=%s"
                                 % (r.returncode, r.stderr, r.stdout))
        out = json.loads(r.stdout) if r.stdout else None
        with open(pp, "rb") as f:
            after = f.read()
        tmps = [n for n in os.listdir(d) if n.startswith("pack.json.tmp.")]
        return out, after, tmps, pp, d.__enter__() if False else d


class Op27(unittest.TestCase):
    def call(self, op_obj, pk=None, expect_rc=0):
        pk = pk if pk is not None else pack()
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            pp = os.path.join(d, "pack.json")
            with open(pp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(pk, f)
            before = open(pp, "rb").read()
            r = subprocess.run([sys.executable, RELAY, "config", pp,
                                json.dumps(op_obj)], capture_output=True,
                               text=True)
            self.assertEqual(r.returncode, expect_rc,
                             "rc=%s err=%s out=%s"
                             % (r.returncode, r.stderr, r.stdout))
            out = json.loads(r.stdout) if r.stdout else None
            after = open(pp, "rb").read()
            tmps = [n for n in os.listdir(d) if ".tmp." in n]
            return out, before, after, tmps

    def test_preview_pass_render_and_key_order(self):
        topo1 = json.loads(json.dumps(base_topo()))
        topo1["links"][4]["bandwidth"] = 50  # peak 40/50 = 0.8
        op = [27, 0, 0, [[1, topo1, P]], [flow()], SCENARIOS, 1000000]
        out, before, after, tmps = self.call(op)
        self.assertEqual(list(out.keys()),
                         ["op", "mode", "status", "old", "new", "applied",
                          "events", "config"])
        self.assertEqual([out["op"], out["mode"], out["status"],
                          out["old"], out["new"], out["applied"]],
                         [27, 0, 0, 0, 1, False])
        self.assertEqual(after, before)  # preview writes nothing
        self.assertEqual(tmps, [])
        row = out["events"][0]
        self.assertEqual(list(row.keys())
                         if isinstance(row, dict) else None, None)
        e, status, old, new, impact = row
        self.assertEqual([e, status, old, new], [1, 0, 0, 1])
        self.assertEqual(len(impact), 4)
        old_worst, new_worst, delta, scenarios = impact
        self.assertEqual(old_worst, [None, "0.400000"])
        self.assertEqual(new_worst, [None, "0.800000"])
        self.assertEqual(delta, "+0.400000")
        self.assertEqual(len(scenarios), 3)  # no-failure, x, z
        # no-failure scenario
        s0 = scenarios[0]
        sid, peak, ok, flows, links = s0
        self.assertEqual([sid, peak, ok], [None, "0.800000", True])
        self.assertEqual(flows[0],
                         ["f1", 3, 30, 110,
                          ["n0", "n1", "n3", "n4"], True])
        self.assertEqual(links[4],
                         ["n3", "n4", 50, 40, "0.800000"])
        # scenario x: node n1 down -> via n2, latency 51? no, 50+50+10
        sx = scenarios[1]
        self.assertEqual(sx[0], "x")
        self.assertEqual(sx[1], "0.800000")
        self.assertTrue(sx[2])
        self.assertEqual(sx[3][0],
                         ["f1", 3, 110, 110,
                          ["n0", "n2", "n3", "n4"], True])
        # links incident on n1 still listed with used zero
        by_pair = {(l[0], l[1]): l for l in sx[4]}
        self.assertEqual(by_pair[("n0", "n1")][3:], [0, "0.000000"])
        self.assertEqual(by_pair[("n1", "n3")][3:], [0, "0.000000"])
        # scenario z: explicit directed link n0->n1 removed
        sz = scenarios[2]
        self.assertEqual(sz[0], "z")
        self.assertEqual(sz[3][0][4], ["n0", "n2", "n3", "n4"])
        self.assertEqual(sz[3][0][2], 110)

    def test_commit_then_resend_and_idempotent(self):
        topo1 = json.loads(json.dumps(base_topo()))
        topo1["links"][4]["bandwidth"] = 50
        op1 = [27, 1, 0, [[1, topo1, P]], [flow()], SCENARIOS, 1000000]
        out, before, after, tmps = self.call(op1)
        self.assertTrue(out["applied"])
        self.assertEqual(out["status"], 0)
        self.assertNotEqual(after, before)
        self.assertEqual(tmps, [])
        saved = json.loads(after)
        self.assertEqual(saved["v"], 1)
        # exact resend against the advanced pack: status 1, no rewrite
        pk1 = pack(topo1, v=1, history=[[0, base_topo(), P],
                                        [1, topo1, P]])
        out2, _, after2, tmps2 = self.call(
            [27, 1, 0, [[1, topo1, P]], [flow()], SCENARIOS, 1000000],
            pk=pk1)
        self.assertEqual([out2["status"], out2["old"], out2["new"],
                          out2["applied"]], [1, 0, 1, False])
        self.assertEqual(after2, after)
        self.assertEqual(tmps2, [])
        # idempotent event (same t/p as current): row status 1, [] impact
        out3, _, after3, _ = self.call(
            [27, 1, 1, [[2, topo1, P]], [flow()], SCENARIOS, 1000000],
            pk=pk1)
        self.assertEqual(out3["status"], 0)
        self.assertEqual(out3["events"], [[2, 1, 1, 1, []]])
        self.assertEqual(after3, after)

    def test_latency_violation_fails_gate(self):
        topo2 = json.loads(json.dumps(base_topo()))
        topo2["links"][2]["latency"] = 51
        topo2["links"][3]["latency"] = 51
        # x scenario now routes n0-n2-n3-n4 = 112 > maxLatency 110
        op = [27, 1, 0, [[1, topo2, P]], [flow()], SCENARIOS, 1000000]
        out, before, after, tmps = self.call(op)
        self.assertEqual(out["status"], 2)
        self.assertEqual([out["old"], out["new"], out["applied"]],
                         [0, 0, False])
        self.assertEqual(after, before)
        self.assertEqual(tmps, [])
        row = out["events"][0]
        self.assertEqual(row[0:4], [1, 2, 0, 0])
        scenarios = row[4][3]
        self.assertTrue(scenarios[0][2])          # no-failure still fine
        self.assertFalse(scenarios[1][2])         # x violates latency
        fx = scenarios[1][3][0]
        self.assertEqual(fx, ["f1", 3, 112, 110,
                              ["n0", "n2", "n3", "n4"], False])
        self.assertTrue(scenarios[2][2])          # z only 112? same path
        # z shares the n2 path: 112 > 110 too
        self.assertFalse(scenarios[2][3][0][5])

    def test_unreachable_renders_null_row_and_rejects(self):
        # candidate deletes n2; under scenario x (n1 down) n0 cannot
        # reach n3 at all
        topo3 = {"nodes": ["n0", "n1", "n3", "n4"],
                 "links": [link("n0", "n1", lat=10),
                           link("n1", "n3", lat=10),
                           link("n3", "n4", lat=10)]}
        op = [27, 1, 0, [[1, topo3, P]], [flow()], SCENARIOS, 1000000]
        out, before, after, tmps = self.call(op)
        self.assertEqual(out["status"], 2)
        self.assertEqual(after, before)
        self.assertEqual(tmps, [])
        scenarios = out["events"][0][4][3]
        self.assertFalse(scenarios[1][2])
        self.assertEqual(scenarios[1][3][0],
                         ["f1", None, None, 110, [], False])
        # topology-order links of the candidate side; n2 links gone
        pairs = [(l[0], l[1]) for l in scenarios[1][4]]
        self.assertEqual(pairs,
                         [("n0", "n1"), ("n1", "n3"), ("n3", "n4")])

    def test_overload_fails_gate(self):

    return {"nodes": ["n0", "n1", "n2", "n3", "n4"],
